newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks pare losses at close on late buying.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks pare losses at close on late buying.

text.p: Thai stocks pared losses at the close on Friday, after declining nearly two percent earlier in the day, on local mutual fund buying of blue-chip finance and bank issues, brokers said.
The SET index fell 0.14 point by the close to 932.86 on 4.5 billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index remained unchanged at 70.08-point.
"Late bargain-hunting on large capitalised finance and banking stocks helped move the index up before the market closed," said Thaneit Khantigaroon of Ekachart Finance and Securities.
"It was believed that the buying of stocks, especially those blue-chip finance and banking issues, was made because they were considered cheap," Thaneit said.
The finance counter slipped 1.62 percent while the property sector was down 1.52 percent and the banking sector gained 0.05 percent at the close.

The main index fell heavier earlier in the day following a sell off on rumours, which hit the market on Thursday, that property developer Somprasong Land faced cash problems. The company later denied the rumours.
Somprasong Land fell its limit earlier in the day and stayed that way until the close, down 1.25 baht to 11.25.
National Finance and Securities topped the active list, declining 3.50 baht to 50.50. Krung Thai Bank declined 1.50 to 80.50 and Bangkok Bank gained one to 188.
Italian-Thai Development, a major construction firm, slipped one baht to 131.
Today's market close at a more than three-year-low prompted brokers to say that support for the index was seen at 916 while resistance would be at 950 on Monday.
